title: Practice 10: Which prefix? — the whole table, as practice

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Tom flew to Australia.
exercises.why: **улетел** is the past tense (masculine) of **улететь** (to fly away, to depart (by flying); (figuratively) to be carried away or transported in thoughts or feelings) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **улетать**. past: он улете́л · она улете́ла · оно улете́ло · они улете́ли. — Wiktionary, «улететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choices: **вылетел** (**вылететь**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **отлетел** (**отлететь**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **слетел** (**слететь**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: A mouse came into the room.
exercises.why: **вбежала** is the past tense (feminine) of **вбежать** (to come running in, to come rushing in, to run (into)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **вбегать**. past: он вбежа́л · она вбежа́ла · оно вбежа́ло · они вбежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «вбежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **выбежала** (**выбежать**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **пробежала** (**пробежать**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something; **убежала** (**убежать**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Tom is going on tour.
exercises.why: **уезжает** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **уезжать** (to go away, to drive off, to leave, to depart (by vehicle)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **уехать**. present: я уезжа́ю · ты уезжа́ешь · он уезжа́ет · мы уезжа́ем · вы уезжа́ете · они уезжа́ют. — Wiktionary, «уезжать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choices: **выезжает** (**выезжать**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **заезжает** (**заезжать**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **проезжает** (**проезжать**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: A cat came out from under the desk.
exercises.why: **вылез** is the past tense (masculine) of **вылезть** (to get out, to climb out, to get off; (of hair) to fall out, to come out) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **вылезать**. past: он вы́лез · она вы́лезла · оно вы́лезло · они вы́лезли. — Wiktionary, «вылезть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **влез** (**влезть**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **залез** (**залезть**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **слез** (**слезть**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Tom converted to Catholicism.
exercises.why: **перешёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **перейти** (to cross, to get over, to get across; to pass on (to), to proceed (to), to turn (to)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **переходить**. past: он перешёл · она перешла́ · оно перешло́ · они перешли́. — Wiktionary, «перейти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "пере-" implies the following meanings: a) Going across or over something. In this case the verb is commonly followed by the preposition через + Acc. However, sometimes this preposition is omitted and the verb takes a direct object: Мы перешли через улицу. Мы перешли улицу. — We crossed the street. b) Moving from one place to another. In this case the verb may be followed by any preposition indicating motion to or from a place: Мы переехали на другую квартиру. — moved to … Мы переехали из города в деревню. — moved from … to …» — DLI, Lesson 62.  Compare: «Студент переходит через улицу.» (Imperfective, present) — DLI, Lesson 62. «Танки медленно переходили через поле.» (past) — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **вышел** (**выйти**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **дошёл** (**дойти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **подошёл** (**подойти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: She gave me a ride home.
exercises.why: **довезла** is the past tense (feminine) of **довезти** (to take (to), to carry (as far as, to), to bring (to, as far as)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **довозить**. past: он довёз · она довезла́ · оно довезло́ · они довезли́. — Wiktionary, «довезти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**до-** — Reaching a limit or destination Example: Пассажиры доехали до последней остановки и вышли из автобуса. — The passengers reached the last station and exited the bus. Prepositional phrases: до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «"Going verbs" with prefix "до-" indicate motion up to a certain point and may mean: a) going as far as …; b) reaching of a destination. Я доехал до угла и повернул направо. (went as far as…) У меня было мало бензина, но я всё-таки доехал до города. (reached the destination) These verbs are always followed by the preposition до + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **вывезла** (**вывезти**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **перевезла** (**перевезти**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **провезла** (**провезти**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Let's go out on the terrace.
exercises.why: **выйдем** is the future tense (1st person plural) of **выйти** (to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **выходить**. future: я вы́йду · ты вы́йдешь · он вы́йдет · мы вы́йдем · вы вы́йдете · они вы́йдут. — Wiktionary, «выйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  The other choices: **перейдём** (**перейти**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **подойдём** (**подойти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach; **придём** (**прийти**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: He's a little slow on the uptake.
exercises.why: **доходит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **доходить** (to come to, to arrive at, to reach (usually by foot); (by extension) to finally or eventually get to, to achieve some state or condition) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **дойти**. present: я дохожу́ · ты дохо́дишь · он дохо́дит · мы дохо́дим · вы дохо́дите · они дохо́дят. — Wiktionary, «доходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**до-** — Reaching a limit or destination Example: Пассажиры доехали до последней остановки и вышли из автобуса. — The passengers reached the last station and exited the bus. Prepositional phrases: до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «"Going verbs" with prefix "до-" indicate motion up to a certain point and may mean: a) going as far as …; b) reaching of a destination. Я доехал до угла и повернул направо. (went as far as…) У меня было мало бензина, но я всё-таки доехал до города. (reached the destination) These verbs are always followed by the preposition до + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  Compare: «Мы обычно доходим до этой остановки, а дальше едем на трамвае.» (Imperfective, present) — DLI, Lesson 62. «Во время дождей вода доходила до нашего дома.» (past) — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **входит** (**входить**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **выходит** (**выходить**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **отходит** (**отходить**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Tom drives Mary to school.
exercises.why: **отвозит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **отвозить** (to take away (by vehicle), to drive away, to take (someone or something by vehicle)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **отвезти**. present: я отвожу́ · ты отво́зишь · он отво́зит · мы отво́зим · вы отво́зите · они отво́зят. — Wiktionary, «отвозить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. Antonym: под- Example: Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца, который предложил ему конфеты. — The boy stepped back from the stranger who had offered him candy. Prepositional phrases: от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Verbs of motion with the prefix от- denote moving away from an object, a place or a person and require the preposition от + genitive case: Я отхожу от автомобиля. Студент отходит от учителя. Грузовик отъезжает от магазина.» — DLI, Lesson 29.  «отвозить — отвезти — to take (haul) to отводить — отвести — to take (lead) to. Note that the verbs "относить", "отвозить" and "отводить" are seldom used as opposites of the verbs with the prefix "под-". Their most common meaning is: "to take an object (or person) to a certain place and leave it there". Thus:.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «Note that the verbs "относить", "отвозить" and "отводить" are seldom used as opposites of the verbs with the prefix "под-". Their most common meaning is: "to take an object (or person) to a certain place and leave it there".» — DLI, Lesson 79.  Compare: «Я отвёз деньги в банк.» (I took (by vehicle) money to the bank.) — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choices: **ввозит** (**ввозить**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **довозит** (**довозить**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **увозит** (**увозить**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The sun came out from behind the clouds.
exercises.why: **вышло** is the past tense (neuter) of **выйти** (to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **выходить**. past: он вы́шел · она вы́шла · оно вы́шло · они вы́шли. — Wiktionary, «выйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  The other choices: **дошло** (**дойти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **подошло** (**подойти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach; **прошло** (**пройти**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Can I come backstage?
exercises.why: **пройти** (the infinitive) (to pass, to go, to walk; to pass by) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проходить**. — Wiktionary, «пройти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "про-" implies the following meanings: a) Going through — через + Acc.: Мы проехали через лес. b) Passing by — мимо + Gen.: Мы прошли мимо вашего дома. c) Passing between — между + Instr.: Войска противника прошли между лесом и рекой. d) Covering a distance — verb + Acc.: Они прошли два километра. e) Passing (missing) a place or leaving it behind — verb + Acc.: Мы проехали нашу станцию. (missed it) Мы уже проехали этот город. (left it behind) Notice also the following expressions: Прошла неделя. — A week went by. Дождь прошёл. — The rain stopped.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **отойти** (**отойти**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **прийти** (**прийти**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion; **уйти** (**уйти**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: I want to retire.
exercises.why: **уйти** (the infinitive) (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **уходить**. — Wiktionary, «уйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choices: **обойти** (**обойти**) has the prefix о-, об-, обо- — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place; **отойти** (**отойти**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **сойти** (**сойти**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: We're leaving in five minutes.
exercises.why: **выезжаем** is the present tense (1st person plural) of **выезжать** (to exit, to go out (by vehicle); to break in (a horse)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **выехать**. present: я выезжа́ю · ты выезжа́ешь · он выезжа́ет · мы выезжа́ем · вы выезжа́ете · они выезжа́ют. — Wiktionary, «выезжать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs въезжать (to drive in) and выезжать (to drive out) belong to the 1st ("-е-") type of conjugation (like читать): я въезжаю, ты въезжаешь … они въезжают.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  The other choices: **доезжаем** (**доезжать**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **переезжаем** (**переезжать**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **приезжаем** (**приезжать**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: He walks the children to school.
exercises.why: **отводит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **отводить** (to lead away; to take / draw aside) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **отвести**. present: я отвожу́ · ты отво́дишь · он отво́дит · мы отво́дим · вы отво́дите · они отво́дят. — Wiktionary, «отводить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. Antonym: под- Example: Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца, который предложил ему конфеты. — The boy stepped back from the stranger who had offered him candy. Prepositional phrases: от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Verbs of motion with the prefix от- denote moving away from an object, a place or a person and require the preposition от + genitive case: Я отхожу от автомобиля. Студент отходит от учителя. Грузовик отъезжает от магазина.» — DLI, Lesson 29.  «отводить — отвести — to take (lead) to. Note that the verbs "относить", "отвозить" and "отводить" are seldom used as opposites of the verbs with the prefix "под-". Their most common meaning is: "to take an object (or person) to a certain place and leave it there". Thus:.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «Note that the verbs "относить", "отвозить" and "отводить" are seldom used as opposites of the verbs with the prefix "под-". Their most common meaning is: "to take an object (or person) to a certain place and leave it there".» — DLI, Lesson 79.  Compare: «Я отвёл сына в школу.» (I took (walked with) my son to school.) — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choices: **выводит** (**выводить**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **доводит** (**доводить**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **сводит** (**сводить**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: We walked out of the movie.
exercises.why: **вышли** is the past tense (plural) of **выйти** (to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **выходить**. past: он вы́шел · она вы́шла · оно вы́шло · они вы́шли. — Wiktionary, «выйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  The other choices: **перешли** (**перейти**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **пришли** (**прийти**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion; **ушли** (**уйти**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: We'll drop you off on the way.
exercises.why: **завезём** is the future tense (1st person plural) of **завезти** (to take (to a place), to drop off (at a place); to supply, to deliver) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **завозить**. future: я завезу́ · ты завезёшь · он завезёт · мы завезём · вы завезёте · они завезу́т. — Wiktionary, «завезти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "за-" implies the following meaning: (a) Getting (disappearing) behind something — заходить, зайти за + Acc.: Солнце заходит за облака. Автомашина заезжает за дом. (b) Dropping in on somebody or stopping by at a certain place: заходить, зайти — в магазин, на почту, к учителю. (c) Dropping in or stopping by to fetch something or someone — заходить, зайти за + Instr.: Я зайду за вами. — I'll stop by to pick you up. Он зашёл за книгой. — He dropped in to pick up the book. Also note the combination of subparagraphs (b) and (c): Он зашёл ко мне за книгой. — He stopped by at my place to pick up the book. Я заехал на почту за письмами. — I stopped by at the post office to get my mail.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **вывезем** (**вывезти**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **довезём** (**довезти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **увезём** (**увезти**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: This doesn't fit in the box.
exercises.why: **влезает** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **влезать** (to get into (something, also figurative), to climb into, to scramble into; to fit in, to go in) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **влезть**. present: я влеза́ю · ты влеза́ешь · он влеза́ет · мы влеза́ем · вы влеза́ете · они влеза́ют. — Wiktionary, «влезать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **вылезает** (**вылезать**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **залезает** (**залезать**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **слезает** (**слезать**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: It's too late now, Lusya!
exercises.why: **ушёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **уйти** (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **уходить**. past: он ушёл · она ушла́ · оно ушло́ · они ушли́. — Wiktionary, «уйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choices: **дошёл** (**дойти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **обошёл** (**обойти**) has the prefix о-, об-, обо- — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place; **подошёл** (**подойти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Tom walked away from the restaurant.
exercises.why: **ушёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **уйти** (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **уходить**. past: он ушёл · она ушла́ · оно ушло́ · они ушли́. — Wiktionary, «уйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choices: **отошёл** (**отойти**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **перешёл** (**перейти**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **пришёл** (**прийти**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: They've crossed the road.
exercises.why: **перешли** is the past tense (plural) of **перейти** (to cross, to get over, to get across; to pass on (to), to proceed (to), to turn (to)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **переходить**. past: он перешёл · она перешла́ · оно перешло́ · они перешли́. — Wiktionary, «перейти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "пере-" implies the following meanings: a) Going across or over something. In this case the verb is commonly followed by the preposition через + Acc. However, sometimes this preposition is omitted and the verb takes a direct object: Мы перешли через улицу. Мы перешли улицу. — We crossed the street. b) Moving from one place to another. In this case the verb may be followed by any preposition indicating motion to or from a place: Мы переехали на другую квартиру. — moved to … Мы переехали из города в деревню. — moved from … to …» — DLI, Lesson 62.  Compare: «Студент переходит через улицу.» (Imperfective, present) — DLI, Lesson 62. «Танки медленно переходили через поле.» (past) — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **вошли** (**войти**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **обошли** (**обойти**) has the prefix о-, об-, обо- — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place; **сошли** (**сойти**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
